caption:
Everything that happened in the shipping industry in the last 24 hours (22 Nov 2026) 🚢

1. Brent holds at $92.57 before OPEC+ meeting
2. Two more tankers hit off Khasab - no casualties
3. Drone hits Russian ship SPARTA II - 16 crew
4. Hormuz attacks up 50% - 2 missing, 13 injured
5. GAS HUSKY sinks - 19 Filipino crew rescued
6. LA-Long Beach watchmen strike averted
7. Samsung plans nuclear-powered LNG carrier
8. Hanwha wins $272m VLCC pair order
9. India scraps ship age limits for its fleet

Sources are credited on each slide. Follow @jaimarineshorts for daily shipping news.

stories.headline: Brent holds at [$92.57] before OPEC+ meeting
stories.summary: Brent crude settled at $92.57 a barrel on Friday, up 0.64% on the day but down 3.41% for the week. It was the third weekly fall in a row. WTI ended near $83-84. Recovering Middle East supply and forecasts of a 2027 surplus outweighed Iran strike fears. OPEC+ meets on 29 November to set 2027 output.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Alf van Beem / Wikimedia Commons (CC0)

stories.headline: Two more tankers hit off Khasab - [no casualties]
stories.summary: UKMTO reported two tanker incidents near Oman on Saturday, 21 November. One tanker was hit at the stern about 20 km north of Khasab, another in the engine room about 31 km east. No casualties were reported. Iran's navy claims a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine east of the strait - not confirmed.

stories.headline: Drone hits Russian ship SPARTA II - [16 crew]
stories.summary: The Russian-flagged ro-ro SPARTA II was hit by a suspected drone on 21 November, about 50 km west of Gogland in the Gulf of Finland. The US-sanctioned ship lost steering and drifted into Finnish waters while burning. Its 16 crew were reported moving into rescue craft. Finland linked the strike to Ukrainian drones - not confirmed by Kyiv.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · kaʁstn Disk/Cat / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0 de)

stories.headline: Hormuz attacks up 50% - [2 missing, 13 injured]
stories.summary: Orbital Risk Intelligence counted 15 attacks and piracy incidents in seven days, up 50% week on week. Four tankers were hit within 13 nm of Khasab in three days. On NAVIG8 MESSI, ADNOC confirmed one crew missing and 11 injured. LPG tanker TARA GAS was hit twice and abandoned. JMIC keeps the Hormuz threat level at SEVERE.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Official U.S. Navy Page from United Stat / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

stories.headline: GAS HUSKY sinks - [19 Filipino crew rescued]
stories.summary: All 19 Filipino seafarers of the LPG tanker GAS HUSKY are safe after the ship sank in Bulgaria's waters in the Black Sea. They were found in a life raft and lifted out by a Bulgarian military helicopter. Two have minor injuries and are staying in Varna. The captain says drones may have hit the ship - cause under investigation.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Geof Sheppard / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

stories.headline: LA-Long Beach watchmen [strike averted]
stories.summary: The Pacific Maritime Association reached a tentative deal on 21 November with ILWU Local 26, which represents about 250 security officers at Los Angeles and Long Beach ports. This averts a strike after talks of more than a year. The deal still needs a member vote. More than 110 trade groups had urged both sides to settle.

queries: Port of Long Beach container terminal

stories.photo_credit: Representative · Jules Verne Times Two / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

stories.headline: Samsung plans [nuclear-powered LNG carrier]
stories.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries and US firm Tesser Atomics signed an agreement on 19 November to develop the world's first nuclear-powered LNG carrier. It would use Tesser's Triton molten-salt reactor and sail between the US and Europe. There is no firm order, cost or schedule yet. The IMO aims to adopt its nuclear code by 2030.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Gordon Leggett / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

stories.headline: Hanwha wins [$272m] VLCC pair order
stories.summary: Hanwha Ocean has signed a contract for two VLCCs worth about $272 million, for delivery by September 2029. Brokers link the order to Switzerland-based Advantage Tankers, whose orderbook now reaches 24 ships. Hanwha has won 47 orders worth $8.54 billion this year, including 24 VLCCs. The price is the highest in about 15 years.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · kees torn / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)

stories.headline: India scraps [ship age limits] for its fleet
stories.summary: India's Directorate General of Maritime Administration removed the compulsory retirement age for Indian-flag ships, effective immediately. Earlier, tankers and bulkers had to leave service at 25, gas carriers and container ships at 30. Ships over 20 years can now join Indian trade. Extra inspections still apply to older tankers, container ships and gas carriers.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Jules Verne Times Two / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
